_comment: Prerequisite pathways: ordered routes through the catalog. Each step names candidate series ids in order of preference (the first that exists in the build is used; 'all' lists several that belong together), or a shelf, a page or a single video. Hand-written; the site resolves them at load time, so a step whose course disappears is skipped rather than broken.

pathways.name: From zero to the brain
pathways.for: You want to understand the brain and have never taken a psychology or biology course.

steps.label: Start with the whole field
steps.why: A first psychology course gives you the vocabulary everything else assumes: perception, memory, learning, emotion, disorders.

steps.label: Behavior from the biology up
steps.why: Sapolsky's Stanford course is the most recommended lecture series in psychology: evolution, genes, hormones and neurons as causes of behavior, with no prerequisites.

steps.label: A real neuroscience course
steps.why: Neurons, neurotransmitters, the senses, motor systems, memory, emotion: NYU's undergraduate course in syllabus order.

steps.label: How the human brain is organized
steps.why: Kanwisher's MIT course on what we know about the human brain specifically: faces, places, language, number, theory of mind.

steps.label: See the classic cases
steps.why: Aphasia, neglect, blindsight, split brains: the patients whose deficits revealed the architecture.

steps.label: Then: the research frontier
steps.why: Seminar series where working neuroscientists present their own results. Not peer-reviewed; treat each talk as one lab's account.

pathways.name: Clinical psychology: from the textbook to the room
pathways.for: You are interested in mental illness and psychotherapy and want the science before the practice.

steps.label: Start with the whole field
steps.why: Disorders and treatment make more sense once you know how normal perception, memory and emotion work.

steps.label: Abnormal psychology
steps.why: The disorders, their diagnosis and what is known about their causes, as a full course.

steps.label: The psychiatric side
steps.why: A psychiatry department's own introductory course: assessment, the major syndromes, medication.

steps.label: Watch an assessment
steps.why: Simulated psychiatric interviews filmed for medical students: what a clinician actually asks.

steps.label: Watch therapy being done
steps.why: Full sessions and role-plays from training institutes: CBT, person-centred, motivational interviewing, and the Shostrom films.

steps.label: Then: grand rounds
steps.why: Hospital grand rounds and clinical colloquia, where clinicians present cases and new evidence to each other.

pathways.name: Clinical neuropsychology
pathways.for: You want to understand what brain damage does to the mind, and how it is examined at the bedside.

steps.label: A neuroscience course first
steps.why: You need the systems before the syndromes: NYU's Brain and Behavior, or Sapolsky's course if you prefer behavior first.

steps.label: The neurological examination
steps.why: UCD's bedside series: the examination step by step, then real patients with Parkinson's, MS, epilepsy and Huntington's disease.

steps.label: The classic cases on film
steps.why: The aphasias, hemispatial neglect, prosopagnosia, blindsight, agnosia, alien hand, phantom limbs, locked-in syndrome, Phineas Gage.

steps.label: Where the functions live
steps.why: Kanwisher's course on the functional organization of the human brain is the map the cases are drawn on.

steps.label: Memory and its loss
steps.why: A full course on memory, the function neuropsychology has studied longest.

steps.label: Then: the clinical neuroscience seminars
steps.why: Oxford's clinical neurosciences department and Cambridge's Zangwill Club: current work, presented by the people doing it.

pathways.name: Cognitive science
pathways.for: You are coming from computer science, linguistics or philosophy and want the mind as an information-processing system.

steps.label: Start with the whole field
steps.why: Cognitive science borrows its questions from psychology; a first course shows you which ones.

steps.label: Cognitive science as a discipline
steps.why: What the field is, where it came from and how its six parent disciplines fit together.

steps.label: Cognitive psychology proper
steps.why: Attention, memory, categories, problem solving: the experimental core.

steps.label: Language
steps.why: Psycholinguistics and language acquisition, the cognitive-science problems that started the cognitive revolution.

steps.label: Philosophy of mind
steps.why: The conceptual questions underneath: representation, consciousness, what a mind is.

steps.label: Then: the field talking to itself
steps.why: Conference sessions and seminar series from the Cognitive Science Society and the Rotman Institute.

pathways.name: Computational neuroscience
pathways.for: You can handle calculus and a little differential equations and want to model neurons rather than just name their parts.

steps.label: The biology you will be modelling
steps.why: A neuroscience course first; the models are only interesting once you know what they are models of.

steps.label: Gerstner's Neuronal Dynamics, module by module
steps.why: Wulfram Gerstner's EPFL course, the standard first course in the subject: from the integrate-and-fire neuron to population dynamics. Take the modules in order.

steps.label: Neuroscience meets machine learning
steps.why: Summer schools where the two fields are taught together.

steps.label: Then: the seminars
steps.why: Theoretical neuroscience seminars and the Cognitive Computational Neuroscience conference.

pathways.name: Methods, statistics and the replication crisis
pathways.for: You want to be able to tell a solid finding from a fragile one.

steps.label: How psychology experiments are built
steps.why: Research methodology for psychology: designs, measurement, validity, the ways studies go wrong.

steps.label: The statistics
steps.why: A full statistics course for psychology students, from distributions to inference.

steps.label: Research and data analysis, Berkeley style
steps.why: A research-methods course taught with real data analysis.

steps.label: What held up and what did not
steps.why: Every contested finding in the catalog with its replication status and the papers behind it.

steps.label: Then: the originals
steps.why: Read the famous experiments against their actual films and papers.

pathways.name: Social and personality psychology
pathways.for: You are interested in how people influence each other and why they differ.

steps.label: Start with the whole field
steps.why: Social and personality psychology sit on top of cognition and emotion.

steps.label: Social psychology
steps.why: Conformity, persuasion, attribution, groups, prejudice: a full course.

steps.label: Personality
steps.why: Traits, their measurement and their biology, and the major theories.

steps.label: Social cognition
steps.why: How people think about people: an advanced course.

steps.label: The famous studies, in their original footage
steps.why: Robbers Cave, Asch, Milgram, the Stanford prison experiment and what became of each.

pathways.name: Consciousness and the mind
pathways.for: You want the hard problem, but with the neuroscience attached.

steps.label: Start with the whole field
steps.why: Perception, attention and memory are where the science of consciousness begins.

steps.label: Philosophy of mind
steps.why: The positions and the arguments, from dualism to illusionism.

steps.label: The neuroscience of consciousness
steps.why: A full lecture course on the neural basis of consciousness: anaesthesia, sleep, blindsight, split brains, the theories.

steps.label: The patients
steps.why: Blindsight, split brains, alien hands and locked-in syndrome, on film.

steps.label: Then: the debate
steps.why: Seminar series where philosophers and neuroscientists argue it out.

pathways.name: How minds develop
pathways.for: You are interested in children, parents or how a mind gets built.

steps.label: Start with the whole field
steps.why: Development is every other topic, on a timeline.

steps.label: Developmental psychology
steps.why: Infancy to adolescence: perception, attachment, language, theory of mind.

steps.label: Language acquisition
steps.why: How children learn language, the developmental problem with the most data.

steps.label: When development goes wrong
steps.why: Developmental psychopathology: autism, ADHD, anxiety and conduct problems across childhood.

steps.label: The original films
steps.why: Gesell's infant films, the Strange Situation, the visual cliff and Piaget, with their papers.

steps.label: Then: the research institutes
steps.why: The UC Davis MIND Institute's lecture series on neurodevelopmental conditions.
